caption_or_description: Stages of resonance (blue arrows indicate sound waves traveling to the right). (a) The first compression meets the tuning fork and gives it a tiny and momentary push. (b) The fork bends and then (c) returns to its initial position just at the time a rarefaction arrives and (d) overshoots in the opposite direction. Just when the fork returns to its initial position (e), the next compression arrives to repeat the cycle. Now the fork bends farther because it is moving.

caption_or_description: In 1940, four months after being completed, the Tacoma Narrows Bridge in Washington State was destroyed by wind-generated resonance. A mild gale produced an irregular force in resonance with the natural frequency of the bridge, steadily increasing the amplitude of vibration until the bridge collapsed.
